findings.summary: The transport reservation releases pooled response memory from its accounting while grpc still retains it, and its DATA-capacity proof also omits padding.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/91/reader-contract.md:167-184 defines 4*Q+256KiB from retained payload/object capacity and an exact invariant containing only live leases, calls and decoded candidates; :186-190 returns call/lease credit once codec buffers are free and ConnEnd arrives. None of the listed options replaces grpc's default buffer pool. Pinned grpc1.85.0 dialoptions.go:726 selects mem.DefaultBufferPool(); mem/buffer_pool.go:42-47 has 4KiB/16KiB tiers; internal/mem/buffer_pool.go:240-261 allocates tier capacity and Put stores it in sync.Pool. mem/buffers.go:155-180 shows Free returns the response backing slice to that pool, rather than releasing retained storage. ConnEnd in internal/transport/http2_client.go:1108-1112 neither purges nor accounts for it. A full response fragmented into approximately4093 1025-byte DATA frames fits the4096-frame ingress cap and can leave approximately16MiB of 4KiB-tier backing after the call unwinds. Subsequent16KiB-frame page calls use another tier, while the invariant admits retained D and new calls as though the old tier had disappeared; no GC/pool-drain condition or persistent cache reservation is specified. Separately, http_util.go:549-594 allocates from fh.Length before stripping padding: a length1025 padded frame with padSize255 retains769 bytes in4096 capacity. transport.go:155-162 evaluates Len, so these frames reset compaction instead of being coalesced. A source-flow arithmetic trace for a512KiB message plus permitted backlog retains752 such roots: backing plus root/handle, raw-fragment and queue-entry minima total3,159,520 bytes versus the stated raw+4Q+256KiB component3,145,728 bytes, before rounding/extra capacity. This disproves that component's claimed proof; it alone is not asserted to prove a whole64MiB overflow because other reserved slack can mask it.
findings.fix: Specify an explicit allocation policy for the pinned client, rather than assuming Free/ConnEnd removes pool retention. The existing exported experimental.WithBufferPool accepts a guard-local mem.BufferPool without a fork/internal import: use an exact-capacity noncaching policy or keep bounded cached capacities charged globally across calls and cleanup until actually dropped/reused. Re-derive DATA/fragment/backlog and compaction charges using actual allocated capacity including padding; update E(R)/concurrency only as needed. Add the future real-HTTP2 fixture for alternating1025-byte/16KiB frame tiers across completed calls, and padded1025-byte frames with255 padding, with charged cached/live capacity and subsequent credit reuse asserted. Preserve the existing receive caps and authority rules.
